rejectedEdges.reason: Reversed relation direction: n-32-4 (the parable of the ship) is introduced by Socrates to explain and support Adeimantus' observation in n-32-3 (the public indictment that philosophers seem useless), but the relationship in the dialogue is Socrates addressing and explaining Adeimantus' objection; more specifically, as categorized, n-32-4 answers or challenges the claim of roguery/uselessness being inherent to the philosopher, or in the current edge scheme Source n-32-4 -> Target n-32-3 as 'supports' misrepresents the dialectical flow where Adeimantus' challenge motivates Socrates' parable.

Reversed or misplaced edge relation: n-34-3 introduces the four faculties of the soul, building upon the contrast of reason and understanding in n-34-2, so n-34-2 develops into n-34-3 rather than n-34-3 developing n-34-2.
Reversed or inappropriate edge type across roles: dialogue passage n-31-4 is claimed to 'support' Jowett's editorial commentary n-8-4, whereas the commentary node analyzes/summarizes the dialogue.
Incorrect edge relation type: n-33-5 (dialogue analogy of the sun) does not 'define' n-9-1 (commentary summary of the sun analogy).
Incorrect edge relation type: n-33-6 (dialogue presentation of the divided line) does not 'define' n-9-2 (commentary summary of the divided line).

value.notes: Reviewed candidate nodes and edges against cited text passages. The substantive textual summaries and attributions of the nodes are well grounded in the Platonic text. Several cross-chunk edges connecting dialogue nodes to editorial commentary summaries incorrectly used 'defines' or 'supports' across ontological source roles, and internal developmental directions on the Line faculties were inverted.
